title: CSS Pixel to Physical Pixel Rasterizer Sandbox
description: Inspect magnified physical device pixel coverage for a 1 CSS-px line at fractional offsets across devicePixelRatio values.
js: var root = document.getElementById('sandbox-root'); var cv = document.getElementById('grid'); var out = document.getElementById('readout'); if (root && cv && out) { var dpr = parseFloat(root.dataset.dpr || '2'); var rawOff = parseFloat(root.dataset.cssoffset || '0.5'); var snap = root.classList.contains('snap-device'); var effOff = snap ? Math.round(rawOff * dpr) / dpr : rawOff; var physStart = effOff * dpr; var physWidth = 1 * dpr; var physEnd = physStart + physWidth; var ctx = cv.getContext('2d'); var cols = Math.ceil(4 * dpr); var cellW = cv.width / cols; var cellH = 84; var topY = 28; ctx.clearRect(0, 0, cv.width, cv.height); for (var i = 0; i < cols; i++) { var overlap = Math.max(0, Math.min(i + 1, physEnd) - Math.max(i, physStart)); if (overlap > 0) { ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(56, 189, 248, ' + (0.15 + overlap * 0.8) + ')'; ctx.fillRect(i * cellW + 1, topY + 1, cellW - 2, cellH - 2); } ctx.strokeStyle = '#334155'; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.strokeRect(i * cellW, topY, cellW, cellH); ctx.fillStyle = '#94a3b8'; ctx.font = '10px monospace'; ctx.fillText(Math.round(overlap * 100) + '%', i * cellW + 4, topY + cellH + 16); } ctx.strokeStyle = '#f59e0b'; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.strokeRect(physStart * cellW, topY - 4, physWidth * cellW, cellH + 8); var frac = Math.abs(physStart - Math.round(physStart)); var crisp = frac < 0.001 && Math.abs(physWidth - Math.round(physWidth)) < 0.001; out.textContent = 'DPR: ' + dpr + 'x | physical range: [' + physStart.toFixed(2) + ', ' + physEnd.toFixed(2) + '] px | raster: ' + (crisp ? 'CRISP (integer-aligned)' : 'BLURRED (subpixel anti-alias)'); }
expectedObservation: At fractional physical coordinates (such as 0.25 CSS px on 2x DPR -> 0.50 device px), the 1 CSS-px stroke straddles adjacent physical pixels at 50% coverage, producing anti-aliased blur. Snapping to Math.round(offset * dpr) / dpr aligns the amber bounds onto integer device pixels at 100% coverage.
